Key among these are the presence of both significant necrosis (NCR Volume (mL) of 19.429) and contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL) of 22.719). The enhancement margin is thick (>3mm), which is also a hallmark of IDH-wildtype gliomas, particularly glioblastoma. These features collectively argue against an IDH-mutant glioma, which typically presents as a non-enhancing, non-necrotic lesion with more circumscribed margins. The mild quality of enhancement is a minor point but does not outweigh the definitive presence of necrosis and enhancement.

The combination of both enhancement and necrosis is the classic imaging signature of a grade 4 glioma. All other features, such as the large tumor volume, extensive edema, and deep infiltration, are also consistent with a high-grade, aggressive tumor.
